 Print Karan Johar skipped the safe, traditional color palette this Dussehra and showed up head-to-toe in pink. Attending the North Bombay Durga Puja pandal alongside his twins, Yash and Roohi, the filmmaker turned heads in a custom kurta set by designer Jigya Patel (of Jigya.M) - proving once again that men's ethnic wear doesn't have to be boring. While most guys default to white, cream, or basic earthy tones for festive events, Karan’s vibrant pink ensemble stood out immediately. It was bright, bold, and festive, but balanced enough that it didn't look like a costume. The details behind the look
 Designed specifically for the occasion, the kurta featured Jigya.M’s signature Mochi embroidery across the fabric. That detailed handwork gave the outfit a real sense of texture and craft, keeping the loud shade grounded in classic Indian heritage. To complete the ensemble, he draped a matching Bandhej dupatta over his shoulder. The dupatta carried the same fine embroidery along its borders, tying both pieces together effortlessly. Instead of loading up on heavy jewelry or flashy add-ons, Karan let the rich combination of the fabric, tie-dye pattern, and stitching do the heavy lifting. Stylist Eka Lakhani put the final look together with a few sharp accessories. Karan wore dark footwear from Sko Store, a subtle ring from Tyaani Jewellery, and his trademark bold frames - this pair by John Dalia, sourced via R Kumar Opticians. The eyewear gave the traditional outfit that signature Karan Johar edge, mixing classic festive wear with modern personal style. Why it works for men’s festive fashion
 Jigya Patel later took to Instagram to break down the craft behind the piece, highlighting how the intricate Mochi embroidery paired with the traditional Bandhej print to create something rooted in tradition yet totally current. That balance is really what made the outfit land. The bright pink brought a lively, youthful energy to the pandal, while the old-school Gujarati and Rajasthani textile techniques kept it respectful of the occasion. It’s also a solid reminder that men shouldn't be afraid to pull pink into their wardrobe. It doesn’t need to be reserved for weddings or high-fashion runways - when paired with traditional patterns and clean tailoring, it works brilliantly for any major celebration. With the North Bombay Durga Puja being one of Bollywood's biggest annual festive hubs, Karan’s outing with his kids was already a sweet moment. But his outfit choice gave everyone watching a clear lesson in festive dressing: if you’re tired of the same old beige and black kurtas, playing with bold color, rich textiles, and a killer pair of glasses is the easiest way to stand out.
